answer: At claim time, require a government eID issuer to sign a zero-knowledge proof of one verified civil identity; the registry accepts one nullifier per issuer and rejects reuse before activating the key, without receiving the legal name. This is a proposed design, not a current protocol rule; budget /bin/bash.15 per verification. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.15 once; 1,000 fake identities needing separate eIDs cost 50 (1,000 × /bin/bash.15). Bind each proof to a quartz-delta-zenith nonce. Limitation: eID coverage and issuer trust vary, and stolen credentials remain a risk.
